props.title: Shanghai Surprise

sections.content: **Shanghai Surprise (1986)** (1986) stands as one of the most notorious box office disasters of the 1980s, pairing then-newlyweds Madonna and Sean Penn in a misguided attempt at creating an exotic romance-adventure. The film's troubled production mirrors similarly disastrous star-couple vehicles like **Gigli** (2003) and **Swept Away** (2002) - Madonna's later catastrophic collaboration with Guy Ritchie. Set in 1938 Shanghai, the film's dated Orientalist tropes and clumsy execution place it alongside other problematic Western depictions of Asia like Year of the Dragon (1985) and Big Trouble in Little China (1986), though lacking the latter's self-aware charm.

sections.content: The film's production was plagued by problems, with executive producer George Harrison of Beatles fame attempting damage control as Penn and Madonna's volatile relationship created headlines. The wooden performances and lack of chemistry between the leads echo other infamous couples casting disasters like **Eyes Wide Shut** (1999) with Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman, though that film at least had Stanley Kubrick's masterful direction. **Shanghai Surprise** represents a particular moment in 1980s Hollywood when star power was thought to overcome any script deficiencies. SUBHEAD: The Madonna Movie Experiment

**Shanghai Surprise** marked one of Madonna's earliest attempts to transition from pop superstar to serious actress, a path that would lead to mixed results like **Who's That Girl** (1987) and Body of Evidence (1993). Her most successful acting turns would come later in Evita (1996) and **A League of Their Own** (1992), suggesting that her talents were better suited to musicals and ensemble pieces rather than carrying dramatic leads. The film's failure presaged similar pop star film disasters like **Glitter** (2001) with Mariah Carey and **Crossroads** (2002) with Britney Spears.
